article.title: Paramount's acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery is on hold
article.summary: The bidding war for Warner Bros. Discovery was won by Paramount Skydance, which forced Netflix to drop out. The deal has however been put on hold by a judge. Twelve US state attorneys general requested a temporary restraining order to block Paramount Skydance from closing the deal, and US District Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin of the Northern District of California granted the request. The deal is now effectively on hold for the next 14 days. On August 3, the judge will hold a hearing on the state attorneys general's motion for a preliminary injunction, which would freeze the deal until...

article.title: Nintendo says users voluntarily paid higher prices, have no right to tariff refunds
article.summary: Nintendo urged a court to dismiss a lawsuit demanding that it pass tariff refunds on to customers, saying that people who bought a Switch console or other products have no legal right to refunds that Nintendo is due to receive from the government. Nintendo said in a motion to dismiss yesterday that plaintiffs are "ask[ing] this Court to invent a legal duty out of whole cloth to retroactively re-price completed sales simply because the legal landscape has changed." Nintendo said the plaintiffs "have no legal entitlement to the tariff refunds Nintendo stands to receive." The lawsuit was filed in April by two customers who seek to represent a class of all US residents who bought Nintendo products from February 2025 to February 2026. article.title: Nintendo tells customers it doesn’t owe them a cut of its tariff refunds
article.summary: TL;DR Nintendo has basically told its customers that it won’t give them a cut of its tariff refunds. The company hiked prices in August last year due to increased tariffs imposed by the Trump administration. Gamers filed a lawsuit claiming that Nintendo should give them a share of its tariff refunds since they bought its products at hiked prices. If the Trump administration’s reciprocal tariff scheme wasn’t bad enough for US consumers, Nintendo is about to make it even worse. The Switch 2 maker has basically told its customers it doesn’t owe them any refunds for the extra money they had to pay due to increased tariffs. article.title: French Social Media Ban Kicks Off Wave of New Rules in the EU
article.summary: After months of debates across the continent, France became the first European Union member to ban social media for young teenagers this week, kicking off what’s set to be a wave of new regulations and pressuring the bloc to find a unified approach toward the big tech platforms.

article.title: OpenAI built support agents for its own customer service line, now it hopes big enterprises will trust them too
article.summary: The general consensus emerging across the AI and industrial spheres is that the models themselves are no longer the bottleneck — they are more than good enough to power deep conversations, produce vast swathes of production-grade code, and resolve all manner of customer support requests. The harder problem is everything wrapped around the models: the policies that decide what an agent can do on its own, the escalation path for when it can’t, and the record showing what happened when something goes wrong. article.title_zh: OpenAI 為自家客服構建支援 agent，現在希望大企業也能信任它們
article.summary_zh: AI 和工業領域的共識是模型本身已不再是瓶頸，足以支持深入對話、生成大量生產級代碼並解決各種客戶支援請求。

Samsung has been running One UI 9 betas for the Galaxy S26 series for a while now.
